title: Database indexes
explain: Why can an index make a database lookup faster?
defend: Why should we not index every column?
transfer: A log table receives frequent inserts and rare searches by timestamp. What would you measure before adding a timestamp index?
lesson: An index is an additional lookup structure. It can reduce rows examined for suitable queries, but needs storage and maintenance during writes. The planner may prefer a scan when many rows match. Compare representative query plans and read/write timings before choosing an index.
activity: Draw the path of one lookup and one insert with an index.

title: Transactions
explain: What does a transaction protect when transferring money between accounts?
defend: What can go wrong if the debit succeeds but the credit fails?
transfer: Two customers try to buy the last ticket. Explain why a transaction alone may not prevent overselling and what additional control you would consider.
lesson: Atomicity groups operations so they commit together or are rolled back. Isolation governs concurrent transactions; guarantees depend on the isolation level. Use appropriate locking, constraints, or serializable execution and retry handling for concurrent invariants. A transaction does not automatically remove every race.
activity: Write the invariant that must hold after a transfer.

title: Data normalization

defend: What goes wrong when a customer address is copied into every order and updated inconsistently?
transfer: A receipt must preserve the address at purchase time. Would you always replace that address with a link to the current customer address? Explain.
lesson: Normalization reduces redundant facts and update anomalies by modeling dependencies. An order can reference a customer. title: Password storage
explain: Why should an application avoid storing plaintext passwords?
defend: Why is a fast general-purpose hash insufficient for password storage?
transfer: An attacker obtains a user database containing password hashes. How do unique salts and an appropriate work factor change the attack?
lesson: Use a dedicated password hashing scheme with a unique salt and suitable work factor. A salt prevents identical passwords from sharing the same stored hash and defeats reusable precomputed tables. Cost makes guessing more expensive; it does not make weak passwords unguessable. Do not invent a password hashing scheme.
activity: Contrast encryption, a fast hash, and password hashing.

title: Caching and freshness
explain: How can a cache reduce response time?
defend: What happens when the original data changes but the cache does not?
transfer: Would you use the same cache policy for a product photo and available stock during checkout? Explain.
lesson: A cache reuses stored responses or computed data. It can reduce latency and work but introduces freshness and invalidation choices. title: Algorithmic complexity

defend: Can an O(n) algorithm be slower than an O(n log n) algorithm on a small input?

title: Authentication and authorization
explain: How does authentication differ from authorization?
defend: Does being logged in mean a user can access every record?
transfer: A user changes an invoice ID in the URL and sees another customer’s invoice. Where should the access check happen?
lesson: Authentication establishes identity; authorization decides permitted actions on resources. Enforce access checks on the server for each relevant resource and request.
